text:
ajay: Heads-up — hit a repro that shows steady memory growth + intermittent head-of-line stalling on the continuous-batching codepath when contexts go long (>32k). Logs point to KV pager thrash and a kernel fallback.

devin: Hmm. Can you paste the profiler output + the exact run command?

ajay: Repro command:
```
./run_repro --model redwood-14b --ctx 65536 --batching continuous --qps 150 --duration 300
```

ajay: Small perf dump (shortened):
```
kv_page_faults/sec: 312
kvcache_fragmentation: 82%
cont_batch_merge_wait_ns (p95): 18_200_000
kernel_selected: aten_gpt_fast -> aten_gpt_slow (switch at seq=16384)
mem_growth_mb over run: +430MB
```

maria: That fragmentation number is alarming. Sounds like repeated page evictions while batches are merging. If the merge path holds the head batch mutex while waiting on a page, everything behind it stalls.

tanya: Is this the same as the old HOL (head-of-line) we saw a while back? Any shared state between the merge code and the pager thread?

ajay: Not identical — older HOL was due to synchronous KV reads inside the token loop. Current repro shows async pager requests, but merge code does a synchronous remap (rebind) step when two batches join, which can block if a page is missing and triggers a sync page-in. So hybrid async+sync -> unexpected blocking.

oz: TL;DR: continuous-batching merges can transiently take ownership of a KV region, then call rebind which may synchronously fault. That locks the head-of-line merge and blocks all coalesced requests.

devin: Can we make rebind non-blocking (schedule page-in and return a 'pending' handle) so other batches can continue? Or gate merge until we have a fast-path that guarantees no page faults?

ajay: Quick experiment: made rebind asynchronous + added a small read-ahead for neighboring slots. Local microbench (synthetic long-context) shows tail latency p95 drop from 420ms -> 290ms and mem growth stabilizes. Need to validate at scale.

maria: Nice. We should also look at kernel selection churn — profiler shows switch from aten_gpt_fast to slow path around seq=16384, likely because KV misses change sequence-length distribution heuristics used during kernel selection. If kernel flips mid-request that could amplify head stalls.

ajay: Good catch — trace snippet:
```
TRACE: request=0x7f.. seq=16000..16500 -> kernel=aten_gpt_fast (up to seq16384) -> aten_gpt_slow fallback at 16385
reason: kv_cache_miss_ratio > 0.25
```

tanya: So two orthogonal problems: (1) merge path sync rebind blocking pages, (2) kernel selection switching due to dynamic miss ratio. Both interact and make tail worse.

oz: Proposed next steps:
- Make rebind fully async with a per-batch retry backoff (non-blocking).
- Add optimistic merge: only merge batches whose pages are fully resident or have a pending async fetch.
- Add metric kvcache.merge_block_ms and alert at >1s.
- Add unit/system test that simulates heavy page-in latencies and validates no HOL stall.

devin: I'll add a perf test to eng-runtime CI that runs the repro (reduced scale) and asserts no p99 regressions and bounded mem growth.

maria: I'll create a canary rollout with the async rebind change + metric gating. If p99/tail looks good after 24h, promote.

ajay: Uploaded artifact with full perf traces and heap diff: https://artifacts.internal/redwood/runs/1799123456/trace.tar.gz — contains perf map, kv pager logs, and heap hist.

runtime-bot: deploy triggered: PR#3421 -> staging (async-rebind) :rocket: — monitoring enabled (kvcache.merge_block_ms, kvcache.page_faults).

tanya: Thanks everyone. If anyone wants to help validate the repro at scale, ping me — I'll provision a dedicated staging shard.

oz: Also adding a short-term mitigation: lower the merge aggressiveness threshold when fragmentation > 70% (avoid creating very large merged batches that trigger many page-ins).

devin: Good. We should document this interaction in the perf playbook (kvcache + batching section) so oncall can triage similar regressions faster.

ajay: Will follow up with a short PR that contains the repro + suggested test harness. Marking this thread for postmortem if it regresses in prod. :eyes:
